comments.content: `Collection::reject()`/`unique()` preserve the original array keys, so `$originalOrders[0]` is not guaranteed to exist: if the first order is `$qualifiedKeyName` and gets rejected (e.g. orders `['users.id' => asc, 'name' => asc]`), the collection is `[1 => ['column' => 'name', ...]]`, and reading index `0` raises an "Undefined array key 0" warning, which Laravel's error handler converts into an `ErrorException` — failing the whole export job on PostgreSQL. The same access also fails for raw orders (`orderByRaw()`), which have no `column`/`direction` keys. Use `first()`/`shift()` (which also reindexes) and validate the keys the same way the loop below does.

`$query->getQuery()->orders` can also contain raw orders (`orderByRaw()`, `inRandomOrder()`, etc.), which have no `column`/`direction` keys. The re-apply loop below deliberately guards this case with `blank($order['column'] ?? null)`, but here the first element is read without any guard. On pgsql that raises `Undefined array key "column"` / `"direction"` (Laravel's error handler converts this warning into an `ErrorException`, so the export job fails), and even if the error is not thrown, `reorder(null)` clears all orders, leaving `orderedChunkById()` to page without any `ORDER BY`. Filter out orders without a usable column/direction before selecting the first one.
comments.suggestion_code:
$originalOrders = collect($query->getQuery()->orders)
                ->reject(fn (array $order): bool => blank($order['column'] ?? null) || blank($order['direction'] ?? null))
                ->reject(fn (array $order): bool => in_array($order['column'] ?? null, [$qualifiedKeyName]))
                ->unique('column');
